nodes.name: Biosynthesis of bio-NiFeS
nodes.procedure: The rinsed cells [D. vulgaris Hildenborough] were inoculated into the nitrogen gas-purged mineral medium at an initial optical density (OD600) of 0.4. Then, the stock solution of ferric chloride (FeCl3, 200mM) with final concentration of 0.4mM was injected, followed by adding the stock solution of nickel chloride (NiCl2, 200mM) with final concentration of 2.0mM (Fe/Ni molar ratio 1:5). All serum bottles were incubated at 30°C in a shaker (200rpm). After 22-h incubation, the deposits containing bacterial cells and black precipitates were collected by centrifugation, washed twice using ultrapure water (10,000g,6min), and freeze-dried in a vacuum freeze dryer for 24h.

nodes.name: Annealing of bio-NiFeS
nodes.procedure: In order to promote the electrocatalytic performance of the biosynthetic metal sulfides, the dried samples were annealed in a tube furnace under argon atmosphere and maintained at set temperatures (200~400°C) for 2h, followed by cooling to room temperature.

nodes.name: Biosynthesis from real wastewater
nodes.procedure: A certain volume of anaerobic actual nickel-containing wastewater was added to the serum bottle inoculated with D. vulgaris Hildenborough at OD600 of 0.4, providing final Ni2+ concentration of 2.0mM, and Fe3+ was supplied with final concentration of 0.4mM (Fe/Ni 1:5). Then the bottles were incubated at 30°C in a shaker (200rpm) for 22h. The obtained black powders were collected, rinsed, freeze-dried prior to annealing treatment (300°C, 2h, argon).

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM reveals spherical nanoparticles of 30-40 nm with lattice fringes of 0.231 nm and 0.192 nm corresponding to (101) and (102) facets of Ni0.96S.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The TEM images (Fig. 3B and C) show abundant spherical nanoparticles with sizes of 30~40 nm... HRTEM image (Fig. 3D) reveals the well-resolved lattice fringe spacings of 0.231 nm and 0.192 nm, corresponding to (101) and (102) facets of Ni0.96S.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD shows peaks at 30.2°, 34.6°, 45.7°, 53.6° for Ni0.96S (100), (101), (102), (110) facets and 31.4° for Fe0.95S1.05 (002) facet in bio-NiFeS.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XRD spectra of both the bio-NiFeS and bio-NiS show distinct peaks at 30.2°, 34.6°, 45.7° and 53.6°, corresponding to the (100), (101), (102) and (110) facets of Ni0.96S... a peak at 31.4° corresponding to the (002) facet of Fe0.95S1.05 was detected in the bio-NiFeS.

The Ni2p spectrum (Fig. 4B) reveals the presence of both Ni2+ (870.4 eV and 853.0 eV) and Ni3+ (872.9 eV and 855.1 eV). The Fe 2p spectrum (Fig. 4C) confirms the existence of Fe2+ (723.5 eV, 710.1 eV and 706.8 eV) and Fe3+ (725.3 eV and 711.9 eV). The S2--species is verified by the S 2p spectrum (162.3 eV and 161.2 eV).
